---
title: "Naming Conventions"
order: 5
---

### N1 — Python identifiers follow PEP 8

The linter and every reader expect it. snake_case for variables, functions, and modules. PascalCase for classes. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants.

```python
rt_min = 0.1                 # variable: snake_case
RT_MAX = 2.0                 # constant: UPPER_SNAKE
def clean_trials(raw): ...   # function: snake_case
class SaccadeModel: ...      # class: PascalCase
```

### N2 — R identifiers follow the tidyverse style

A dot means an S3 method, so avoid dots. snake_case for variables and functions. Skip dots in new names. PascalCase for R6 and S4 classes.

```r
rt_min <- 0.1                       # snake_case
clean_trials <- function(raw) { }   # snake_case
# avoid: clean.trials  (dot = S3 method)
```

### N4 — Shell: snake_case locals, UPPER_SNAKE exported

Hyphens are illegal in shell variable names. Local variables and functions use snake_case. Environment and exported variables use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.

```bash
DATA_ROOT=/mnt/labshare      # exported: UPPER_SNAKE
clean_trials() {             # function: snake_case
  local raw_file="$1"        # local: snake_case
}
```

### N5 — Constants and classes are cross-language

Keep the shouted categories recognizable. Constants and environment variables are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE in every language. Classes and types are PascalCase in every language.

```
UPPER_SNAKE_CASE   constants, env vars   (all languages)
PascalCase         classes, types        (all languages)
```

### N6 — Filesystem names are lowercase

Data/ and data/ collide across machines. Lowercase every file and directory name. Linux sees two folders where macOS sees one, and that gap corrupts a shared repo.

```bash
mkdir raw-data        # good
mkdir Raw_Data        # collides on case-insensitive macOS
```

### N7 — No spaces in names

Spaces force quoting and break scripts. Use a hyphen or underscore instead of a space in any file or directory name.

```
eye-tracking-data.csv     # good
eye tracking data.csv     # needs quoting everywhere
```

### N8 — Restrict names to a-z 0-9 - _ .

Other characters are illegal or shell-special. Colons and backslashes are illegal on Windows. The characters & * ? ! carry shell meaning. A leading hyphen looks like a command flag.

```
s01_congruent_v02.csv     # good
s01:congruent (2)!.csv    # illegal on Windows, shell-hostile
```

### N9 — Avoid reserved names, keep paths short

Windows chokes on con, nul, and long paths. Never name a file con, prn, aux, nul, com1, or lpt1. Keep total path length well under 260 characters.

```
reserved on Windows: con prn aux nul com1..com9 lpt1..lpt9
keep the full path under 260 characters
```

### N10 — Repositories and branches use kebab-case

Matches GitHub, URLs, and the ecosystem. Name repositories and git branches in lowercase kebab-case.

```bash
adamolab/eye-tracking-2026         # repo
git switch -c fix-outlier-filter   # branch
```

### N11 — Directories use kebab-case

Readable in a URL and a terminal. Name directories in lowercase kebab-case.

```
saccade-model/
├── raw-data/
├── figure-scripts/
└── clean-output/
```

### N12 — Script files follow language import rules

Python cannot import a hyphenated module. Python and R modules use snake_case so they stay importable. Standalone shell tools use kebab-case, matching how you type the command.

```
data_cleaning.py     # Python module, importable
clean_data.R         # R script
run-analysis.sh      # shell tool, a CLI command
```

### N14 — Config keys use snake_case

They map straight onto code variables. Keys in YAML, TOML, or JSON use snake_case so they line up with the Python and R variables that read them.

```yaml
# config.yml
rt_min: 0.1
n_boot: 10000
data_root: /mnt/labshare
```
